doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: Basie band after Prez, and Buddy Tate
summary: He argues nobody filled Prez's chair in Basie's band, with Rowe naming Buddy Tate.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Exactly. It’s not putting Fred or Buddy down or putting anybody down, it’s just that I’m a different person. And my newest, the “Timely” album, is living proof of hey, you might not like it as well but hey what the hell, it’s what I’m doing now. Somebody likes it because it’s been moving. And I’m still doing it and I’m still playing all over the world, which is cool. But it’s like how many Benny Goodman bands really did it? How many Count Basie bands did it? How many Duke Ellington bands did it? Regardless of the personnel, with very few changes during that era. But it couldn’t — you know, after Prez left Basie? As far as I’m concerned, nobody filled that chair. Even as well as Illinois played, as well as Lockjaw played, you know, whoever was soloing.
Well he filled the other fellas’ chair. Even that was different.
